voice_spoof_detector.note: pretrained inference, no training -- Principle 11 evidence-gate run. WINNER of the 2026-09-02 three-model bake-off over the identical 204 cases; supersedes garystafford/wav2vec2-deepfake-voice-detector, kept at voice_spoof_detector_garystafford_superseded. Beat the incumbent on every axis: recall 0.9500 vs 0.8500, precision 0.9661 vs 0.9107, FPR 0.0476 vs 0.1190, ROC-AUC 0.9836 vs 0.9251. Third challenger (Hemgg/Deepfake-audio-detection) did not load -- a real answer about that checkpoint, not a gap. PROVENANCE: the Colab run had no GITHUB_TOKEN so its metrics.json never reached the repo. Rather than retype the printed output, the confusion matrix is recomputed from the persisted per-case rows (run_id 69916bd3 = train, a1d2bbc8 = held_out): TP=114 FP=4 TN=80 FN=6 over 120 spoof + 84 bonafide -- the 84 bonafide are the shared negative baseline scored in BOTH splits, which is why 288 rows are 204 distinct cases. That reproduces the printed precision/recall/f1/FPR and both split recalls exactly. roc_auc and pr_auc are carried from that same run's output (they need the continuous scores, which the rows do not carry) -- every field around them reconciled, which is why they are trusted. Threshold calibrated via best_f1_threshold on bonafide + train-split spoof only, then applied unchanged to held_out.

voice_spoof_detector_garystafford_supers.note: SUPERSEDED by mo-thecreator/Deepfake-audio-detection, which beat it on every axis over the identical 204 cases. Kept for the record, not for reporting. pretrained inference, no training -- evidence-gate run per Principle 11. Threshold calibrated via best_f1_threshold on bonafide + train-split spoof only (round 2), then applied unchanged to held_out -- round 1 used an uncalibrated 0.5 default.

document_consistency_detector.note: rapidocr (PP-OCR ONNX via onnxruntime-gpu) + our own QR cross-check, no training -- Principle 11 evidence-gate run on Colab T4, n=680 (480 fraud + 200 bonafide). SUPERSEDES the paddlevl n=120 measurement, kept at document_consistency_detector_paddlevl_n120_superseded. PROVENANCE, because this entry was NOT written by the eval script: the 2026-09-01 Colab run scored all 680 cases and persisted one row per case to Supabase evaluation_results, but its metrics.json never reached the repo -- only the A3 cell's printed prose did, so the site kept showing the superseded n=120 paddlevl numbers. Rather than retype that prose, every field here is recomputed from those persisted rows (run_id 0ee2574a-1136-48e8-a45c-ea00f649d6db = train, b605a39b-4c31-4096-8df8-4623a8e8d398 = held_out), which carry the real per-case score and ground truth. The recomputation reproduces A3's printed claims exactly (recall 1.0000, precision 0.9375, FPR 0.1600, 32 false positives), which is why they are trusted. Score is quantized to {0, .25, .5, .75, 1.0} by construction (mismatched-over-comparable across four fields), so roc_auc/pr_auc are computed over those five levels with ties handled at 0.5. Per split: train recall 1.0000 on n=240 fraud, FPR 0.1910 on n=89 bonafide; held_out recall 1.0000 on n=240 fraud, FPR 0.1351 on n=111 bonafide. 16% FPR is still high for production -- reported as measured, not as solved.

document_consistency_detector_paddlevl_n.note: SUPERSEDED by the rapidocr n=680 run -- kept for the record, not for reporting. pretrained OCR-VL + our own QR cross-check logic, no training -- evidence-gate run per Principle 11. Run on Google Colab (T4 GPU), not locally -- paddlepaddle-gpu proved unstable across four distinct low-level Windows driver/library errors in a row (DLL collision, cudnn version mismatch, opencv package collision, cudnn execution failure); see docs/FUTURE_INTEGRATIONS.md item 2. Detector and metrics code run unmodified from the repo. Threshold calibrated via best_f1_threshold on bonafide + train-split fraud only (round 2), then applied unchanged to held_out -- round 1 used an uncalibrated 0.5 default, which is why round 1 showed recall=0.7125 vs round 2's 0.9125 at the same false_positive_rate (0.25 both rounds -- the same 10/40 bonafide docs were misflagged either way; the quantized field-mismatch score never put a bonafide doc exactly between 0.25 and 0.5).

fusion_adversarial_eval.note: Section 6 evidence gate -- weighted XGBoost+LightGBM+Autoencoder fusion, same held-out set as the individual *_adversarial_eval entries, for direct comparison.

reasons: The autoencoder relies on reconstruction error to flag anomalies, but already exhibits a low recall of 0.43 under off-hours and moderate velocity conditions.

Lowering the velocity to 'low' and moving the time to 'business_hours' significantly reduces the statistical anomaly footprint, likely decreasing reconstruction error and allowing stealthier fraudulent transactions to bypass detection.
